identity.description:
E2: one reviewer against the specialist set, and per-case Codex tokens

D4c experiment E2: one reviewer over the whole diff against the specialist set. The note is `docs/research/e2-single-reviewer.md`.

## Result

No line between one reviewer and the specialists is found. For each single arm (Opus 5.5 medium, Opus 5.5 high, Terra high), the 90% bootstrap interval of the line covers the full range of the cases, 12 to 3164 changed lines. Up to about 700 changed lines the data permits a comparison; above 1,000 lines it does not, because the set holds two such cases.

- Under 100 lines, Opus 5.5 at medium posts as many goldens as the specialists (recall 0.444 each), with a higher precision (0.800 against 0.500).
- From 100 to 300 lines, the specialists lead (0.700 against at most 0.575).
- From 300 to 1,000 lines, Opus 5.5 at high leads (0.476 against 0.381), on five cases.
- The reviewer stage of a single Opus arm costs about a third of that of the specialists ($17.83 and $22.29 against $64.06), and takes about three times as long (median 37 s and 53 s against 14 s).

Every arm passes the same verifier (Sonnet 5.5 high, first verifier only, through replay), so the arms are paired. E2 changes no default.

## Changes

- `docs/research/e2-single-reviewer.md`: the note, with the method, the rule test on made-up figures, every figure, the costs and times, the follow-ups and the limits.
- `TICKETS.md`: E2 is done, with two follow-ups (more repeats of the small cases; cases above 1,000 lines from walle and websites before a tier rule by size).
- `pr-review eval-codex-review` now prints the tokens of each case and writes `<out>/tokens.json`, kept across a rerun. Replay reads `<case>.json` by name, so the extra file does not reach it.
- The version goes to 0.19.0.

## Checks

`npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` pass. In one full run, one existing test (`test/eval-by-pass.test.ts`, a bootstrap test) hit its 5 s timeout under load; alone, the file passes 26 of 26.

findings.claim: A case named "tokens" collides with tokens.json: its findings file is overwritten by the token map and is never seen as finished.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a file name that a case name cannot produce, such as `.tokens.json` or a subdirectory, or reject the case name "tokens".
findings.explanation: The case file `<out>/tokens.json` and the token map share one path, so the case output is lost and the case reruns each time.

findings.claim: An error from writeTokens is not caught, so the command throws instead of giving an exit code, and a finished case can turn into a crash.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap writeTokens in try/catch and print a warning.
findings.explanation: reviewCase catches every error, but the new write of the side file can reject (disk full, permissions) and abort the whole run.

findings.claim: The resume rule says a failed case writes no file, but a failed case now writes or updates `<out>/tokens.json`.

findings.explanation: The loop calls writeTokens for every case, failed and quota cases too, so a failed case now changes a file in `--out`.

finding.suggested_fix: Use a file name that a case name cannot produce, such as `.tokens.json` or a subdirectory, or reject the case name "tokens".
finding.explanation: The case file `<out>/tokens.json` and the token map share one path, so the case output is lost and the case reruns each time.

first.rationale: A case named \"tokens\" writes `tokens.json` for its findings. `writeTokens` then overwrites that file, and `finished` excludes it, so the case reruns every time. Nothing rejects the name, but it is an unlikely name for a case.

escalated.rationale: Case names come straight from directory names with no restriction. A case named "tokens" writes `<out>/tokens.json`, then writeTokens replaces that file with the token map. finished() also leaves tokens.json out, so the case never counts as done. This only happens with that one case name, so it is an unusual path.

final.rationale: Case names come straight from directory names with no restriction.
